claim: A remaining owner makes into_inner consume only its own token

claim: Any finite safe trace at arbitrary graph depth stays within two native Drop frames

claim: The proposed edge operation matches a non-recursive safe native step

claim: Every nonempty admitted path decreases rank
boundary: No claim about malformed manually fabricated cyclic Arc graphs

claim: An admitted graph has no payload cycle
boundary: Construction admission is a separate source/test obligation

claim: Published and captured roots are distinct strong owners

claim: Every modeled non-stuttering reclamation step decreases potential

claim: No infinite sequence of modeled non-stuttering reclamation steps exists
boundary: Does not imply an application eventually releases its retained handles

claim: Every modeled Arc lifecycle step preserves strong-count and destruction phases

claim: At any modeled trace length payload destruction is at most once and only after last owner

claim: All variables remain in their declared model domains
boundary: Model-state shape is not directly observable from the public Rust API

claim: Each fixed token is either present or gone
boundary: This partition equation alone is shallow; lifecycle predicates carry the nontrivial safety claim

claim: A node with a remaining strong owner remains live
boundary: Model owner set must correspond to all source owning paths

claim: Each modeled payload is destroyed at most once

claim: Live and destroyed phases agree with strong count and destruction count

claim: Every pending or failed edge belongs to an active native frame

claim: Edge-token location agrees with source payload phase
boundary: Source correspondence must include both edge loops and shared targets

claim: Safe-policy peak node Drop activation count is at most two

claim: Unsafe-policy control should fail when failed Err release becomes the last owner

claim: Every modeled payload has reached the destroyed phase

claim: Unless all payloads are destroyed some non-stuttering model action remains enabled
boundary: TLC enabledness on finite instances does not prove arbitrary-size source enabledness
